questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.learningObjective: Define GDP as the market value of final goods and services produced in a period
questions.stem: A data table lists a country's output for one year; which total equals its gross domestic product?

options.text: The market value of all final goods and services produced within the country during the year
options.misconception: confuses domestic production with national income earned abroad

options.text: The market value of all goods and services including intermediate inputs produced within the country
options.misconception: counts intermediate goods twice in the total

options.text: The total value of all second-hand goods resold within the country during the year
options.misconception: treats resale of used goods as new production

options.text: The market value of all final goods and services produced by the country's citizens anywhere

questions.explanation: GDP measures final output produced within borders in a period. Counting intermediates double counts, resales are not new production, and citizen output abroad belongs to GNP.
questions.hint: GDP is about where production happens, not who produces it.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Value added and the final good
questions.learningObjective: Relate total value added to the final good's price
questions.stem: Explain why summing value added across all stages equals the price of the final good.

answer.exemplar: Each stage adds only its new contribution, so earlier inputs cancel out; the sum telescopes to the final price, which is why GDP counts final value only.

questions.explanation: Value added at each stage subtracts the cost of inputs, so intermediate values cancel telescopically. The sum therefore equals the final good's market price.
questions.hint: Intermediate purchases cancel between stages.
